TITLE: Embraer Q3 2026: operations beat, the profit miss is noise
QUOTE: We delivered record third quarter revenue of $2.3 billion with revenue and margin expansion across all our businesses. Our backlog reached a new all time high of $35.7 billion for the eighth consecutive quarter.
QUOTE_WHO: Francisco Gomes Neto, President and CEO, Q3 2026 earnings call, 10 November 2026
COMPANY_INTRO: Embraer, based in Brazil, builds regional jets, business jets and defence aircraft such as the KC-390, and services their fleets. Commercial jets were 30% of Q3 revenue. Listed in São Paulo and New York.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Beat
TAKEAWAYS.text: Revenue USD 2.35bn (+11% vs. consensus) and adjusted EBIT USD 255m (+22%), a 10.9% margin.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Raised
TAKEAWAYS.text: Free cash flow guide lifted to USD 700m or more, from USD 400m; revenue guide also raised.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Reaction
TAKEAWAYS.text: Shares rose 5.9% intraday on 10 November although adjusted net income missed consensus by 50%.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: 13.1x forward earnings, 9% below the 14.3x average since 2014: the upgrades are not yet priced.

H_P1: Cash, not net income, sets the tone
P1_PARAGRAPH: Revenue beat consensus by 11% and adjusted EBIT by 22%, while adjusted net income fell 50% short, yet the shares rose 5.9% intraday on 10 November. We read the divergence as justified: the miss came from a non-cash revaluation of the share-linked incentive plan and higher tax, while USD 628m of free cash flow and the raised cash guide are recurring.
C1_TITLE: EMBJ3: Q3 2026 surprises vs. consensus and guide revisions
C1_SUB: Q3 lines vs. press-reported consensus (revenue and EBIT in USD, net income in BRL) · FY26 guides vs. the previous guide (revenue midpoint, free cash flow floor)
C1_COMMENT: The operating lines and the cash guide carry the chart; the miss sits below operating profit. Adjusted net income of USD 74m absorbed USD 159m of net financial costs, mainly the incentive-plan revaluation, which rises with the share price. Free cash flow of USD 628m, twice last year’s, came from pre-delivery payments.
BASE_CASE: The case remains very constructive and the risk/reward skewed to the upside. We underwrite an adjusted EBIT margin of about 10% for 2026, rising with mix as business jets and services, at 16% to 17% margins, outgrow commercial jets at 2.4%. The USD 35.7bn backlog, about four years of revenue, gives visibility to 2030. At 13.1x forward earnings, below the long-run average, the rerating has room. The next test is the Q4 print and the 2027 guide.
UPSIDE: Firm orders from the large Indian and European jet campaigns; a Q4 EBIT margin above the implied 9%; business jet output moving toward the 200-unit target for 2028.
DOWNSIDE: Supply delays leaving Q4 short of the 80 to 85 commercial jets guided; commercial margins sliding back toward zero; new-programme spending lifting capex above USD 550m.
H_A1: Results: every division widened its margin
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Revenue rose 17% to USD 2.35bn, a record for a third quarter, and adjusted EBIT 48% to USD 255m, lifting the margin to 10.9% from 8.6%. Commercial aviation grew 13% to USD 696m with a 2.4% margin, helped by supplier compensation. Business jets grew 12% to USD 655m at 16%, about 430bp higher, on price, mix and the absence of last year’s US import tariffs. Defence grew 22% to USD 341m at 15.7% on KC-390 volumes. Services and support grew 30% to USD 638m at 17%, about 330bp higher on operating leverage. Nine-month revenue of USD 6.0bn is above 70% of the guidance midpoint.

The quarter beat on revenue, operating margin and free cash flow and missed on earnings: adjusted net income of USD 74m was 13% below last year and about 50% below consensus, yet the shares rose 5.9% by 10:24 on 10 November. Management named the drivers of the miss: USD 159m of net financial costs, mainly the mark-to-market of the long-term incentive plan, and higher taxes. Neither touches operations or cash. The rise is consistent with investors looking through a charge that grows with the share price, but we cannot confirm positioning: the stock had already gained 16% in the two weeks before the print.
H_A2: Outlook: cash guide up 75%, margins held
A2_PARAGRAPH: Embraer raised its 2026 revenue guide to USD 8.4 to 8.6bn, from 8.2 to 8.5bn, and its adjusted free cash flow guide, excluding Eve, to USD 700m or more, from USD 400m, the second upgrade this year. The 10.0% to 10.6% EBIT margin range and the delivery guides, 80 to 85 commercial and 160 to 170 business jets, are unchanged. After 10.7% over nine months, the range implies about 9% in Q4 at the midpoints, partly as defence margins normalise. Beyond 2026, capex rises to USD 500 to 550m in 2027 and 2028 for the 200-unit business jet target, and Eve, the air mobility unit, should contribute only after 2029.
C2_TITLE: EMBJ3: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: EMBJ3 BZ, weekly, Sep 2014 to 10 Nov 2026, BRL · Bloomberg 12m-forward consensus · 40-week simple MA · log scale · Jan 2019 to Jun 2022 earnings trough blanked and excluded from the P/E average · last price BRL 113.45 is an intraday level on results day
C2_COMMENT: Over 12 months the price rose 31% and consensus EPS 29%, so the move has been earnings-led. At 13.1x 12m-forward earnings, the multiple sits 9% below its 14.3x average since 2014, with the 2019 to 2022 earnings trough excluded, and above its 11.7x one-year average, but well under the 22.1x peak of July 2025. The price is 31% above its 40-week average, a stretched short-term trend. A return to the long-run average would add 9% at unchanged earnings; a 10% EPS upgrade at today’s price would take the multiple to 11.9x.
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, company filings, Embraer Q3 2026 earnings call of 10 November 2026, analyst research notes of 10 November 2026
